title: Separatedness of algebraic spaces tested by universal closedness of the diagonal
statement: Let $B$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and use algebraic spaces over $B$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], with fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. A closed immersion of algebraic spaces means a representable map whose every base change to a scheme is a closed immersion of schemes [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Give the point spaces their quotient topology from surjective etale scheme atlases [def-a1-space-point-topology]. Let $g:U\to V$ be any morphism of algebraic spaces, and let $\Delta_g:U\to U\times_VU$ be its diagonal. Call a morphism universally closed if every algebraic-space base change induces a closed map on point spaces. Then $g$ is separated, meaning that $\Delta_g$ is a closed immersion, if and only if $\Delta_g$ is universally closed. No quasi-compactness or finite type assumption on $g$ is required.

proof.text: If $g$ is separated, its diagonal is a closed immersion by the definition in the statement. Apply [lem-sfb-space-closed-subspace-proper] to $\Delta_g$ over $B$: it is proper and hence universally closed, by the explicit definition of properness in that cited statement. This proves the forward implication.

Conversely suppose $\Delta_g$ is universally closed. Put $W=U\times_VU$ and take any scheme $T\to W$. By [lem-sfb-space-diagonal-scheme-tests], $D_T=U\times_WT$ is a scheme and $d_T:D_T\to T$ is a locally finite type monomorphism. For a scheme $Y$, the point space $|h_Y|$ of [def-a1-space-point-topology] is the underlying space of $Y$: by [def-a1-algebraic-space-point-classes] the map $|\mathrm{id}_Y|:|Y|\to|h_Y|$ sends $y$ to its residue-field point; it is surjective because a field point $\operatorname{Spec}K\to Y$ with image $y$ factors through $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)$, and injective because equivalent field points have a common extension and hence the same image point. A subset is open in the final topology iff its preimage under $|\mathrm{id}_Y|$ is open: $\mathrm{id}_Y$ is one of the etale charts, and conversely the preimage of a Zariski open under any etale scheme map $T''\to Y$ is open. Now $d_T$ is universally closed as a scheme morphism: for every scheme $T'\to T$, the fibre-product universal property [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] identifies $D_T\times_TT'$ with $U\times_WT'$ over $T'$, and the projection $|U\times_WT'|\to|h_{T'}|$ is closed by the assumed algebraic-space universal closedness of $\Delta_g$ along $h_{T'}\to W$; by the identification just made, this is the map of underlying spaces of the scheme projection $D_T\times_TT'\to T'$. This is precisely the scheme definition [def-weil-proper-morphism].

proof.text: For this scheme map $d_T$, [lem-trf-scheme-monomorphism-separated] gives separatedness and [lem-weil-pbc-universally-closed-quasi-compact] gives quasi-compactness. Along with local finite type from step 2, this gives finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], hence properness [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Thus [lem-pc-proper-monomorphism-closed] makes $d_T$ a closed immersion. This holds for every scheme $T\to W$, and the diagonal is representable by step 2. By the stated definition of closed immersions of algebraic spaces, $\Delta_g$ is a closed immersion, so $g$ is separated. The only local finite type assertion used is about the diagonal; none is required of $g$.
